items.reasoning: Value proposition = replace up-front owned capacity with on-demand resources you start and stop
Global reach + speed of deployment: launch in Regions near each market as a config step, no local lease
Capacity following demand up AND down is elasticity; C names the service not the benefit
Well-Architected Framework is the pillars/design-principles review lens; the Tool only records reviews
Operational excellence and Sustainability are pillars; fault tolerance/elasticity/revenue are not
Recovering from disruption and continuing to operate is the Reliability pillar's definition
Adoption is sequenced deliberately under a chosen migration strategy, not one big-bang cutover
Migration Evaluator inventories the current estate and builds the projected business case
CAF business outcomes include reduced business risk and increased revenue
Minutes of cutover with zero lost writes requires ongoing replication/change capture, not a bulk export
Capital purchase of owned capacity becomes variable operating spend tracking consumption
Rack/power/cooling and hardware refresh disappear; compute spend and DB licenses persist
Keeping owned entitlements on AWS compute is Bring Your Own License
Sub-10% utilization with no app change = rightsize the instances to observed demand
Automated provisioning/teardown removes both manual staff effort and forgotten idle spend
Economies of scale: aggregated demand lowers AWS unit cost, passed into pricing
The model divides security OF the cloud (AWS) from security IN the cloud (customer)
Customer owns data classification/access and guest OS patching on EC2
Patch management is the canonical shared control - each party carries it at a different layer
Moving EC2-hosted DB to RDS transfers engine patching to AWS; customer keeps data/access/config
Customer inherits AWS physical/infrastructure controls and gets encryption as a configuration option
Dedicated, customer-controlled validated crypto hardware is CloudHSM
Who/when/from-where for an API change is CloudTrail event history
AWS Artifact is the on-demand self-service source of AWS audit reports/attestations
Compliance program coverage is per service; it must be checked service by service
Discovering and classifying sensitive data in S3 is Macie
Groups apply one permission set to many users; AWS managed policies attach as-is, custom fills gaps
Full admin for a narrow task violates least privilege
MFA on root plus deleting the root access key and using an IAM identity for daily work
Closing the account and changing account name/email are root-only tasks
Secrets Manager stores and returns secrets at run time, off the source file
Cross-account access should be an assumed IAM role, not a pasted long-lived access key
Federation means users authenticate against the existing corporate directory, which stays authoritative
Shield for the DDoS flood, WAF for injection strings in web requests
Standing written analysis of security features/practices is the AWS Security Blog
Third-party security software is procured through AWS Marketplace, no new vendor onboarding
Recurring account hygiene checks (open buckets, no-MFA users) are Trusted Advisor security checks
Identical repeatable stacks = infrastructure as code from one template
Workloads in AWS and on-premises connected privately is the hybrid model
Distant readers need content cached at CloudFront edge locations, not more AZs in one Region
Multi-AZ for single-data-center loss; EU records stored in an EU Region for residency
CPU-saturating job with tiny I/O is compute optimized
Sub-second, event-driven, nothing running between events is Lambda
Fixed pair pinned during surges needs auto scaling to add/remove instances
Managed database transfers patching/backup/availability to AWS; customer keeps data and access
Hundreds of millions of key-value items, single-key reads, no joins = DynamoDB
Heterogeneous engine change: SCT converts the schema, DMS moves the data
Public/private subnet split plus a VPN gateway pair for the office's private path
Subnet-wide, instance-independent source blocking is a network ACL
Predictable contracted throughput over internet-VPN variability is Direct Connect
EFS for shared multi-instance documents; instance store for disposable scratch
Hot for a month then 7-year retention with hours-long retrieval = lifecycle transition to Glacier
One place for retention policy and compliance reporting across EBS/EFS/RDS is AWS Backup
Extracting text and form fields from scanned documents without ML skills is Textract
Ad-hoc SQL directly over S3 files with no cluster is Athena
SQS decouples the slow refund consumer; SNS fans the same event out to all channels
High-volume application-sent email is SES
Finding which internal call is slow within a request is X-Ray tracing
Persistent full desktop with retained settings/files is WorkSpaces; AppStream streams apps only
Secure connection and fleet management for sensors is IoT Core; Kinesis only ingests
Interruption-tolerant, deadline-free, cheapest-possible batch is Spot
Zonal RI discount shares across consolidated billing but only within its AZ: holder's 1 + 3 matching = 4
Data out to the internet and inter-Region transfer are charged; inbound and at-rest storage are not
Estimating a design that does not exist yet is the Pricing Calculator; Cost Explorer is retrospective
Activated cost allocation tags attribute charges per brand; name prefixes do not reach the bill
Basic gives customer service and community resources only; Business adds 24/7 technical support
Accountable paid delivery comes from AWS Professional Services or an APN partner
No plan, no urgency, peer answer wanted = AWS re:Post
